input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The § 12.1 grant runs to "Customer" alone and is expressly "revocable", so IBM may withdraw the licence at its discretion, and neither our Affiliates (defined in the preamble) nor contractors acting on our behalf are licensed, with no notice mechanism to add them. That combination is the rule's walk-away scenario and fails the fallback (affiliates on written notice). Nothing elsewhere cures it: § 14.17 confirms only expressly stated licences are granted, and § 14.19 / § 14.11 further narrow use. Successor transfer is adequately addressed by § 14.10 (assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition), so no change is needed there. Redline deletes "revocable", ties termination of the licence to termination of the Agreement, and extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement. Such license is irrevocable except upon expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 3.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and to contractors using the Services on our behalf, and removed "revocable" so the licence can only end on termination of the Agreement rather than at IBM's discretion. If helpful, we can accept Affiliate coverage on written notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Extend Base Components licence to Customer Affiliates and contractors and remove at-will revocability
